title: LocaleOutput
description: The UI-locale diagnostic `duckduckgo-search-cli locale` writes on stdout. Unlike every other envelope here it carries NO `type` field, so it cannot be routed by discriminator — a consumer identifies it by the subcommand it invoked. That asymmetry is recorded rather than papered over: adding `type` now would be a wire change, and the surface is already reachable only by asking for it explicitly. Added in v1.0.3 (GAP-SCHEMA-INTROSPECTION-UNDECLARED-001). English-only keys; the VALUES describe the resolved UI language, which is a different axis from the SERP language set by `-l/--lang`.

type.description: Envelope discriminator (v1.0.4+). This envelope already carried `strategy: "locale"`, but `strategy` answers HOW the locale was resolved, not WHICH envelope this is — so the catalog had nothing to route on. Emitted by `types::LocaleKind`, a compiler-checked constant.

strategy.description: How the UI language was negotiated, e.g. `locale`.

resolved.description: The UI language actually in force after negotiation.

source.description: Where the winning value came from: the `--ui-lang` flag, XDG config, or the system locale.

system_raw.description: The unnegotiated system locale as read from the host. May be empty when the host reports none.

script.description: Writing system of the resolved language, e.g. `Latn`.

direction.description: Text direction of the resolved language.

available.description: Every UI language this binary can negotiate to. A value outside this list can never be `resolved`.

ui_lang_flag.description: Echoed so an agent reading only this envelope learns which flag changes `resolved`.

search_lang_flag.description: Echoed to prevent the standing confusion between UI language and SERP language: this envelope is about the former, and `-l/--lang` controls the latter.
